chapter: Donaldsonville, family and Richard M. Jones
title: Claiborne Williams band members and Monnie
summary: Brass section players, Monnie in the brass band, the Cal family, and when Monnie left for publishing.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Well, let's see now. Some of the other guys. Buddy Caieri or something like that. I never have known how you pronounce that name. Who? I've seen this written down. K-Y-E-R-I. Buddy Caieri? I don't even know what he played, but he's supposed to play with Clayman Williams.

Maybe he did. It was before my time. Yeah. Well, who did you know in that band? Lawrence Hall was a trumpet player. You got him? I heard the name. He was from the Poemville, but he came up all the time to sit in. And then we had, oh, another, Willie Daly. He died right here. But he didn't play anymore. You ever heard of him? No, I can't remember.
That was Clayman Brass Section. And he played the trumpet. Sullivan Sproul, did you know him? That may have been years ago. I think they got a lot of stuff from Monty himself.

You see, they had a brass band. Monty didn't play in the orchestra. Monty played in Clayman's brass band. Oh, I see. That's what I was told. I don't remember that. I see. You never have heard of Si Cal. I can't play him. He's a piano player. Si, the old man played the trumpet. Tony Cal was the son. That's the one who got great. He got poisoned some. Tony Cal played the piano. Si Cal was the daddy was the cornet player. Oh, I see.
But when you came to New Orleans, was Monty here then? Mm-hmm. He was gone. He was already gone then?

He was already gone then? Yeah, he was in publishing business. There was somebody here. And he left here. I don't know who it was. I wouldn't. I wouldn't want to say it because I don't know. But he left here. He left here way early. Mm-hmm. He was gone.
